title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Regulations on Judicial Police of the People's Courts
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Regulations on Judicial Police of People's Courts

Fa Fa [2012] No. 23

To the high people's courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Regulations on Judicial Police of People's Courts have been deliberated and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court. They are hereby promulgated and shall come into force as of December 1, 2012.

October 29, 2012

Regulations on Judicial Police of People's Courts

Chapter I General Provisions

Article 1 These Regulations are formulated in accordance with the Civil Servant Law of the People's Republic of China, the Organic Law of the People's Courts of the People's Republic of China, the People's Police Law of the People's Republic of China, and other laws, for the purposes of strengthening the construction and scientific management of the judicial police force of the people's courts and ensuring that judicial police exercise their functions and powers according to law.

Article 2 The judicial police of people's courts are one of the police categories of the People's Police of the People's Republic of China.

Article 3 The tasks of the judicial police of people's courts are to prevent, stop, and punish illegal and criminal acts that hinder trial activities, maintain trial order, and ensure the smooth progress of trial work.

Article 4 The Supreme People's Court leads the judicial police work of local people's courts at all levels and special people's courts, and a people's court at a higher level leads the judicial police work of a people's court at a lower level.

Article 5 The judicial police of people's courts must take the Constitution and laws as the norms of their activities, serve the people wholeheartedly, be loyal to their duties, be honest and upright, obey orders, and strictly enforce the law.

Article 6 The judicial police of people's courts perform their duties according to law and are protected by law.

Chapter II Functions and Powers

Article 7 The duties of the judicial police of people's courts are as follows:

(1) maintaining trial order;

(2) conducting security checks on persons entering the trial area;

(3) escorting and guarding the accused or criminals in criminal trials, summoning witnesses and expert witnesses, and transmitting evidence;

(4) cooperating in the implementation of enforcement measures in the compulsory enforcement of effective legal documents, and taking compulsory measures according to law when necessary;

(5) executing the death penalty;

(6) assisting in the safety of the court and the emergency handling of petitions related to lawsuits;

(7) executing compulsory measures such as summons by force and detention;

(8) other duties as provided by laws and regulations.

Article 8 During court trials, the judicial police of people's courts shall, in accordance with the instructions of the presiding judge or the sole judge, forcibly remove from the court, impose fines, or execute detention according to law on those who violate court rules, make disturbances, storm the court, insult, slander, threaten, or assault judicial officers, litigation participants, or other persons, thereby disrupting court order.

When emergencies occur that endanger the personal safety of persons in the courtroom or the escape of the accused or criminals, the judicial police of people's courts shall first take necessary measures.

Article 9 For those who obstruct judicial officers from performing their duties by violence, threats, or other means, the judicial police of people's courts shall promptly control them, conduct inquiries, collect or fix relevant evidence as necessary, and execute compulsory measures such as fines and detention according to law.

Article 10 For those who forcibly enter the trial area where entry is not appropriate, the judicial police of people's courts shall forcibly remove them according to law; for those suspected of illegal or criminal acts, the judicial police of people's courts shall control them and transfer them to the public security organs in a timely manner depending on the circumstances.

Article 11 In the compulsory enforcement of effective legal documents, the judicial police of people's courts may, according to law, cooperate in carrying out enforcement actions such as searches, sealing up, distraint, and compulsory eviction.

Article 12 When, in the course of performing their duties, the judicial police of people's courts encounter parties or other persons committing suicide, self-harm, or other acts, they shall promptly take measures to stop such acts and assist in medical treatment, and when necessary, shall take restraint and protection measures against them, and transfer them to the public security organs depending on the circumstances.

Article 13 For those who seriously disrupt the work order of the people's court, endanger the personal safety of the people's court staff, or the safety of the court's property, the judicial police of people's courts shall take disposal measures such as reprimand, stopping, and controlling, preserve relevant evidence, and for those suspected of illegal or criminal acts, promptly transfer them to the public security organs.

Article 14 In emergency situations such as escape, interception of prison vans, snatching of firearms, or other violent acts, the judicial police of people's courts may use police equipment in accordance with the relevant state regulations; if the use of police equipment cannot stop the situation or if not using weapons may lead to serious consequences, they may use weapons in accordance with the relevant state regulations.

Chapter III Organization and Management

Article 15 The judicial police of people's courts shall implement the police rank system according to law. Personnel to whom people's courts grant police ranks shall use the state's special staffing, hold judicial police positions, and perform judicial police duties.

Article 16 The staffing and organizational structure of the judicial police of people's courts shall be prescribed by the Supreme People's Court.

Article 17 The judicial police of people's courts shall be managed in organized units. The Supreme People's Court shall establish a Judicial Police Bureau, the high people's courts shall establish Judicial Police Corps, the intermediate people's courts shall establish Judicial Police Detachments, and the basic people's courts shall establish Judicial Police Brigades.

Article 18 The judicial police of people's courts shall accept the leadership of the president of the people's court where they serve and the judicial police department of the higher people's court, and accept the management of the judicial police department of the people's court where they serve.

Article 19 The main duties of the judicial police departments of people's courts at all levels in managing the judicial police work at their own level are as follows:

(1) organizing the implementation of regulations, directives, and other relevant documents concerning judicial police;

(2) formulating and implementing rules, regulations, and detailed rules for judicial police work;

(3) organizing judicial police to perform their duties;

(4) organizing education and training for judicial police;

(5) assisting in managing the police ranks of judicial police;

(6) managing equipment for judicial police;

(7) completing other tasks assigned by the court president.

Article 20 The main duties of the judicial police department of a higher people's court in managing the judicial police work of lower people's courts are as follows:

(1) researching and formulating plans and rules for judicial police work;

(2) guiding, supervising, and evaluating judicial police work;

(3) formulating education and training plans for judicial police;

(4) undertaking the filing and recordation of appointment and removal of principal heads of judicial police departments;

(5) managing the police ranks of judicial police;

(6) coordinating major police activities across regions;

(7) undertaking other matters requiring management.

Article 21 Judicial police recruited by people's courts shall meet the conditions prescribed by the state. When recruiting judicial police, people's courts shall, in accordance with state regulations, conduct open examinations, strict assessments, and select the best candidates.

Newly recruited judicial police shall have a probation period of one year. Those who pass the assessment upon expiration of the probation period shall be formally appointed and have their corresponding police ranks evaluated and granted; those who fail shall have their recruitment eligibility revoked.

Article 22 Persons transferred or reassigned to serve as judicial police in people's courts shall meet the conditions for serving as judicial police of people's courts and the qualification requirements for the proposed position.

Article 23 When a people's court allocates its judicial police, it shall seek the opinions of its judicial police department; the appointment or removal of the principal head of the judicial police department shall be reported to the judicial police department of the higher people's court for recordation.

Article 24 Judicial police of people's courts shall undergo professional training for judicial police, and may only take up a post or be promoted, or be granted or promoted in police rank upon passing the examinations and assessments.

Article 25 Judicial police of people's courts shall implement a police post sequence, divided into a police officer post sequence, a police personnel post sequence, and a police technical post sequence.

Article 26 Judicial police of people's courts shall dress in uniform, wear police insignia, maintain a neat and tidy appearance, and behave with dignity.

When performing their duties, judicial police of people's courts shall carry their People's Police Identification Cards.

Article 27 The rewards and punishments of judicial police of people's courts shall be handled in accordance with relevant state laws and regulations and the relevant provisions of the Supreme People's Court.

Chapter IV Police Affairs Guarantees

Article 28 Judicial police of people's courts must execute the decisions and orders of their superiors.

If a judicial police officer of a people's court believes that a decision or order is erroneous, he or she may raise an opinion in accordance with the regulations, but shall not suspend or alter the execution of the decision or order; if the opinion raised is not adopted, he or she must obey the decision or order; the consequences of executing the decision or order shall be borne by the superior who made the decision or order.

Judicial police of people's courts have the right to refuse to execute instructions that exceed the scope of duties of judicial police of people's courts as prescribed by laws and regulations, and shall simultaneously report to the higher authorities.

The execution of instructions from the presiding judge or the sole judge shall be governed by the provisions of the preceding paragraph.

Article 29 The police insignia, standardized uniforms, weapons, and police equipment for judicial police of people's courts shall be uniformly supervised and manufactured by the Ministry of Public Security, and managed by the Supreme People's Court together with the Ministry of Public Security; other individuals and organizations shall not illegally manufacture or sell them.

The police insignia, standardized uniforms, weapons, police equipment, and People's Police Identification Cards of judicial police of people's courts are exclusively for the use of judicial police; other individuals and organizations shall not possess or use them.

Article 30 The funds needed for the work and training of judicial police of people's courts shall be guaranteed and included in the financial budget of the people's court.

Article 31 People's courts shall strengthen the modernization of judicial police equipment, and systematically improve the equipment and facilities necessary for judicial police work, such as command, communication, weapons, police equipment, protection, transportation, and rescue.

Article 32 Judicial police of people's courts shall implement the state civil servant salary system, and enjoy police rank allowances and other allowances, subsidies, pensions, and social insurance and other welfare benefits as prescribed by the state.

Chapter V Supplementary Provisions

Article 33 These Regulations shall be interpreted by the Supreme People's Court.

Article 34 These Regulations shall come into force as of December 1, 2012. The Interim Regulations on Judicial Police of People's Courts promulgated on May 4, 1997 shall be simultaneously abolished.
